answer: Under correlated slashing, identities that act in lockstep pay for each other. Each epoch auditors fingerprint every agent's answers, timing and funding source; identities whose fingerprints cluster share one penalty, and when any member is caught cheating the fine is k squared across a cluster of k, so each added clone raises the farm's exposure. The audit is a lantern swept at random, so no clone knows when it is lit. An unclustered honest agent has a haven: it risks only its own conduct. Faking an oasis of diversity in each clone needs separate work per identity, which a farm can't share.
